title: Compatibility Negotiation Layer & Upgrade Assistant Policy
creator: Marco Reyes
description:
Problem: Serving runtime changes (new request fields, response metadata, behaviour changes) create client churn and risk for customers on LTS channels. Current deprecation and semver guidance lives in scattered playbooks; we need a concrete compatibility negotiation mechanism and an upgrade assistant that reduces migration effort.

Scope:
- Define a lightweight runtime <Compatibility-Level> negotiation header and JSON schema that servers and clients exchange to select behaviour variants (strict, legacy-compat, shimmed).
- Define LTS channel deprecation windows and automated migration signals surfaced to customers.
- Build an Upgrade Assistant CLI (prototype) that analyzes production traffic (anonymized request/response shapes and feature flags) and suggests one of: auto-shim, migration guide, or scheduled deprecation with risk estimates.
- Add server-side adapters that can serve a compatibility shim for common breaking changes for two SDKs (python, js) as proof-of-concept.
- Integrate compatibility checks into CI gating and runtime rollout gates (canary -> ramp -> general availability).

Why this approach: Negotiation reduces blast radius by allowing clients to opt into strict new behaviour only after they have tested it. The Upgrade Assistant lowers manual effort and gives product teams concrete migration timelines tied to observable usage patterns.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: full ecosystem SDK rewrites, long-term multi-language adapter registry (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility-Level header schema v1 defined in a design doc and reviewed
Runtime accepts Compatibility-Level header and routes to behavior variant (legacy|shim|strict) during canary flows
Upgrade Assistant CLI prototype that analyzes a 7-day sample traffic and emits a migration score and suggested shim config
At least two runtime-side adapter shims implemented (python SDK request shape change, js response metadata change) and covered by unit tests
CI gating step that runs compatibility smoke tests against canary and fails if regression thresholds met
Policy doc published with deprecation windows per LTS channel and rollout gate thresholds

comments: 2026-03-02 Marco Reyes: Kickoff meeting notes — agreed to keep header semantics minimal (numeric level + opt-in flags). Action: draft header schema.
2026-03-04 Asha Patel: Design review — PM asked to include signal types for gating (latency p95, 5xx-rate, quality-regression from eval sets). Dropped complex per-field negotiation for v1.
2026-03-06 Lina Chen (Security): Security review stub requested — ensure Upgrade Assistant data pipeline anonymizes and strips PII. Added as dependency.

2026-03-08 Marco Reyes: Prototype header implemented in runtime router. Found ambiguity when clients omit header -> default to 'legacy' behaviour. Decision: explicit opt-in for strict feature flips; default keeps legacy semantics.
2026-03-10 Design feedback from Priya Singh: UI messaging for deprecation windows must include estimated migration cost and recommended window. Added to Upgrade Assistant output.
2026-03-11 Eng review by Jose Alvarez: Adapter shim approach looks good, but noted performance overhead for per-request shims — added microbenchmark task.

2026-03-12 Asha Patel: Canary gating thresholds proposal — fail canary on (1) sustained 5xx increase >0.5% over baseline for 10m, (2) latency p95 regression >15%, (3) quality regression on smoke evals >2% absolute. Open to tuning with SRE.
2026-03-13 SRE (Marta Novak): Asking to add circuit-breaker fallback that re-routes to stable cluster if canary breaches; will provide runbook. Blocker resolved.
